key_insight: Magnetic-field cycling reduces transformation hysteresis in Ni₄₁Co₉Mn₃₁.₅Ga₁₈.₅ by approximately 50–60%, with suppression persisting on a microsecond timescale.
engineering_relevance: Magnetic-history control could reduce hysteresis losses in fast-switching metamagnetic shape memory devices, but field sweep rate must be considered.
method: Use microsecond pulsed-field magnetization to probe transformation kinetics.
Compare initial and field-cycled metastable martensitic states.
Compare microsecond results with millisecond pulsed-field measurements.
evidence_signal: The measurements show approximately 50–60% hysteresis narrowing after cycling and suggest greater sweep-rate sensitivity of the reverse transformation field in metastable martensite.
watch_item: The mechanism remains unresolved: lower effective activation barriers and microstructure-dependent athermal contributions are proposed explanations, not established causes.
paper_title: Magnetic History and Field Sweep Rate Effects on Transformation Hysteresis in $\mathrm{Ni}_{41}\mathrm{Co}_{9}\mathrm{Mn}_{31.5}\mathrm{Ga}_{18.5}$
